name: Wheal Fortune
summary: A tin and copper mine two miles east of Redruth, drowning below 24 fathoms.

performance.drainage: two horse whims with rag-and-chain pumps, horses in relays day and night, lifting to the adit
performance.inflow: about 30 gallons a minute in summer, 50 to 60 in winter (Captain Tregonning's reckoning)
performance.drainage_cost: about £12 a month in horses, fodder and boys

flaws: The whims only just hold the water at 24 fathoms; in a wet spell it rises
The richest tin and copper ground lies below 26 fathoms, under water
notes: 1 fathom = 6 ft. The adit drains by gravity to the valley, so pumps need only lift water to adit level.
